You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the best and brightest in an inclusive, collaborative environment that fosters professional development and success. And you'll know that you're making a difference every day-for companies, for Canada and for the people you work with.

Our student development opportunities include work terms and co-op programs - all designed to give your career a head start. Work terms are typically four or eight months in length and can be counted towards an accredited co-op program with your university.

Our program is also open to new grads who have graduated in the past year.

Teams you may be selected to interview with will vary, and a more detailed team description will be sent to you if you are selected for an interview.

Apply to this pool if you are a student or new grad who is:

Studying or has studied - Computer Science, Business

Technology, Data Science, Data Analytics, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or related

Interested in either development, analytics, software, business analysis, or similar.

Who We Are:

At Xenon Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:XENE), we are committed to providing a brighter future for patients suffering from neurological disorders. Our employees are smart, passionate, dedicated, and driven by their incredibly important work to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines for patients in need. We are looking for great people who thrive in a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and productive culture to join the Xenon team.

What We Do:

We are advancing an exciting portfolio of neurology therapies in our product pipeline, with a focus on commercializing novel treatments for epilepsy. Building upon the positive results and compelling data from our XEN1101 Phase 2b "X-TOLE" study in adult patients with focal epilepsy, our XEN1101 epilepsy program includes multiple Phase 3 clinical trials in patients with focal onset seizures and primary generalized tonic clonic seizures. In addition, based on topline data from our XEN1101 Phase 2 "X-NOVA" clinical trial in adults with major depressive disorder (MDD), we are actively exploring the future development of XEN1101 in MDD and potentially other indications. Our pipeline also includes other early-stage research programs, and we are proud of the leading-edge science coming out of our discovery labs. Backed by a strong balance sheet to support our growth plans, we continue to build a fully integrated, premier neuroscience company with strong discovery, clinical development, corporate, and commercial operations.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Co-op Student, Computational Biology to support the Biology team to build, develop and deploy machine learning powered applications and automated data analysis/signal processing applications through an on-premises cloud infrastructure.

The position will liaison with Research Scientists and IT Network managers to create production grade, user friendly, front-end and back-end code, mostly using Python programming to deploy machine learning applications to an on-premises Linux server.

The successful applicant will have the ability to work independently, good communication skills, be friendly and easy to work with, strong programming experience in Python, and excellent knowledge of deep learning concepts. The ability to train and run deep learning models (imaging datasets, animal pose estimation, etc.) in a Linux environment is required. Familiarity with Plotly's Dash or similar front end visualization/plotting library is also required.

This position reports to a Computational Research Scientist in the Biology group and will work with other Research Scientists in the InVivo/InVitro Pharmacology team and IT Network Infrastructure Managers in the Xenon Burnaby office location.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Ability to build scalable data models, leading to user friendly web-based applications/GUIs in Python using Plotly's Dash (open source), or FastAPI web frameworks.
Use Docker to build, test and deploy applications as containers.
Setup deep learning pipelines including data labeling to create training dataset, model training, model validation and error quantification (mostly pose estimation models).
Communicate effectively with all stakeholders, including presenting algorithm, methods and results to a larger audience.
Write detailed application documentation using professional tools in GitHub pages or similar.
Act in accordance with Company policies, including, for example, the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and ensure policies are understood and followed.
Other duties as assigned.

Experience with data science and machine learning projects with Python using common data science and visualization libraries like Scipy, Plotly's Dash, etc.

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 22-Jan-25 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us

Nova Scotia Environment and Climate Change's role is to protect the environment, human health and animal health through regulatory excellence, conservation, partnership and promotion. The department also coordinates provincial action on climate change and supports the advancement of the clean economy. To achieve this, we strive to develop legislation, regulations and policies, process notifications, applications, and approvals for regulated activities based on sound scientific knowledge and expertise.

Our goal is to educate, inspect and enforce to ensure compliance with legislation and regulations. We also proactively respond to environmental, conservation, animal, and human health risks and work to develop programs and deliver services to enhance protection in these areas.

About Our Opportunity

Working under direction of the Manager, Climate Plan and Strategic Action (CPSA), you will work closely with and support the CPSA team as they work to create the conditions to enable government and non-government partners/stakeholders to advance the actions within the climate change plan and support progress towards the goals within the Environmental Goals and Climate Change Reduction Act (EGCCRA) through knowledge mobilization, strategic evaluation and coordination, and direct program implementation. You will work within a diverse team of professionals and will support various projects.

Primary Accountabilities

In this position, you will work closely with the CPSA team. Your primary accountabilities will include:

Supporting project teams on research, analysis, and policy/program development on climate change strategic priority files. Examples could include:
Contributing to program/resource development for a new portfolio of resources to help connect Nova Scotians to climate-related funding opportunities (both government and non-government) to implement their priority projects.
Responding to inquiries from municipalities, community organizations, businesses, and individuals who are seeking support in identifying potential funding sources.
Assisting with data compilation and analysis for the climate plan annual reporting process.
Preparing presentations, reports, and other materials for senior leadership.
Supporting senior staff on policy/program development by conducting jurisdictional scans or other analysis of climate change strategic priority files.
Occasionally, you will collaborate with other divisions whose policies, and programs intersect with our mandate.
This position may perform other related duties as assigned.

What We Offer

Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career
Engaging workplace: our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies
Countless career paths
Department specific flexible working schedules

Pay Grade: HOURLY

Salary Range: $15.42 - $29.11 Hourly
job_requirements:

Related programs might include Social or Environmental Sciences/Studies, Public Administration, Climate Change, Planning, Economics, Business, or another relevant post-secondary concentration. Enrollment in a graduate-level program (e.g. Master's) is considered an asset. Knowledge of provincial and federal climate change policies, programs and plans is also considered an asset.

job_description:
The Plotkin evolutionary biology lab is looking for a highly motivated team player who will play a key role in helping us achieve our mission of developing transgenic animals for an emerging model organism. The student will assist with various aspects of the project, with emphasis on the establishment of protocols for CRISPR-Cas genome manipulation. Additional duties will involve aquaculture system maintenance housing an exotic marine invertebrate (the ctenophore Mnemiopsis leidyi), while also assisting with supply management. This position offers candidates the chance to be involved in cutting-edge research and gain exposure to novel biology experiments. It presents an ideal hands-on learning opportunity and valuable work experience for individuals interested in research science.

Key duties include:

Maintenance tasks to ensure the optimal functioning of the aquaculture system, including monitoring water quality parameters, food density, and feeding schedules.
Performing various embryology laboratory techniques, including microscopy, microinjection, and gene tagging probe design.
Transforming plasmids into competent bacterial cells
Performing plasmid DNA preparations
Following general laboratory safety procedures
Collaborate with lab personnel to assist in placing orders for lab supplies, tracking shipments, and receiving deliveries accurately.

Duration: position starting in May, for a term of 4 or 8 months (8 months preferred)
Salary: depend on the applicant's prior experience, ranging from $2600-$3100.
job_requirements:
The ideal candidate will:

Communicate experimental results to project leaders in a timely manner
Keep a detailed record of all experimental procedures
Work in a self-directed manner, demonstrate initiative, and be highly self-motivated
Be willing and able to perform focused, repetitive work when needed
Have a strong interest in working in a wet-lab environment
Be ready to learn: Full training will be provided
Have biosafety certifications and/or prior experience in laboratory maintenance, aquaculture, or similar roles. This is preferred but not mandatory, and paid training is offered for this position.
Have excellent organizational skills to manage supply inventory, orders, and lab documentation.
Have flexibility to work on some weekend days if necessary, because the lab animals need daily maintenance (approx 2-4 weekend days a month, e.g. up to 1 weekend day each week or both weekend days for 1-2 weekends a month), and some statutory holidays.

Consider relocating to Caltech University (Pasadena, California) between May-August to work with the Principal Investigator and collaborators. This is a preferred option moreso than a requirement, but the work environment may be favorable for some candidates. A possible extension for Sept-Dec may be considered.

Problem-solving mindset with the ability to troubleshoot basic issues across the full stack.

job_description:
Telesat (NASDAQ and TSX: TSAT) is a leading global satellite operator, providing reliable and secure satellite-delivered communications solutions worldwide to broadcast, telecommunications, corporate and government customers for over 50 years. Backed by a legacy of engineering excellence, reliability and industry-leading customer service, Telesat has grown to be one of the largest and most successful global satellite operators.
Telesat Lightspeed, our revolutionary Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network, scheduled to begin service in 2027, will revolutionize global broadband connectivity for enterprise users by delivering a combination of high capacity, security, resiliency and affordability with ultra-low latency and fiber-like speeds. Telesat is headquartered in Ottawa, Canada, and has offices and facilities around the world.
The company's state-of-the-art fleet consists of 14 GEO satellites, the Canadian payload on ViaSat-1 and one LEO 3 demonstration satellite. For more information, follow Telesat on X and LinkedIn or visit www.telesat.com
Telesat believes in the power of collaboration and the value of in-person interactions. This is why our employees generally work from the office Monday - Friday, with Wednesday as a remote day. This setup fosters brainstorming, problem-solving, and trusted relationships and allows our employees to come together four days a week to collaborate, innovate and thrive!
Telesat is launching a state-of-the-art satellite constellation of highly advanced satellites in low-earth-orbit that will seamlessly integrate with terrestrial networks. The global network will deliver fiber quality throughput anywhere on earth. We are growing quickly and are currently in need of an energetic LEO Satellite Engineering Co-Op student to join our team.
As Satellite Engineering Co-op for the Lightspeed LEO constellation reporting to the Manager, LEO Satellite Bus and Systems Engineering, you will be responsible for the creation of various tools and manuals needed for satellite design, optimization and analysis. Such tools may include: Power subsystem, spacecraft reliability and LEO constellation design. You will also play an integral role in capturing, developing and documenting technical content for the LEO Satellite Engineering team to help maintain our knowledge base.
This position resides within the LEO Satellite Engineering team, and will support the Space Segment development with a focus on the creation of internal engineering tools and content. The ideal candidate has previous experience with programming languages (MATLAB or Python), has a basic understanding of orbits and spacecraft design and is enthusiastic about being part of a team that is diverse and at the top of its game.
Main Responsibilities

Developing satellite system analysis tools and their user manuals, which are used by the LEO Satellite Engineering team

Identifying areas of improvement for existing tools

Participating in internal and external technical discussions related to the design and development of the Lightspeed spacecraft

Liaising with members of the LEO Satellite Engineering team to learn and to develop the required tools

Reviewing and assessing the technical design details of the Lightspeed spacecraft and writing reports to capture progress

Preparing presentations to help showcase the tools that you have developed to external teams

Capturing, developing and documenting technical content for the LEO Satellite Engineering team to help maintain their knowledge base

Education and Experience Required

2nd or 3rd year bachelor's degree in Computer Science/Electrical engineering/Aerospace/Mechanical Engineering

An understanding of satellite orbital mechanics will be an asset

Proven coding experience with software languages such as Python

Experience with MATLAB and Visual Basic will be an asset

Has a foundational understanding of satellite orbits, spacecraft design and satellite communications

Excellent interpersonal and communications (verbal and written) skills

Great team player and problem solver attitude

An independent and self-motivated attitude

Considerable attention to detail

The ability to effectively interface with other parts of the organization in order to help increase knowledge between departments.

Bilingual in English and French an asset (but not required)

Decision Making and Supervision

Ability to make implementation decisions based on project needs and seek input from engineers when appropriate

This role has no direct reports, but will work and interact with multi-disciplinary engineering teams

Working Conditions

Working conditions are typical of an office environment

Work, generally analytical in nature, requires considerable attention to detail

The successful candidate must be able to work in Canada and obtain clearance under the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP)

Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre is very keen on engaging with diverse groups, including Indigenous students, in science, technology, and engineering through professional opportunities, as it values diversity of backgrounds, lenses, knowledges, experiences and perspectives, which enriches and nurtures collaboration and innovation. The merging of knowledge within a team is definitively considered as a strong asset by the organization. City: Victoria

Organizational Unit: Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics

Discover the possible

Anything is possible at the National Research Council (NRC). As Canada's leading research and technology organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada's future and the world.

At the NRC, you'll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You'll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you'll discover what's possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

Project Description

The Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and UV Research (CASTOR) is a planned Canadian-led space observatory which will survey the ultraviolet and blue-optical skies in the 2030s, changing forever our understanding of numerous astronomical and astrophysical events from the birth of stars to their deaths in supernovae, to the rise of supermassive black holes over cosmic timescales. This work is part of the technology development program at HAA to develop the technology for a space-based spectrograph to be flown on the CASTOR mission.

This work will be setting up and operating the Digital Mirror Device (DMD) reliability tests. The DMD is an array of MEMS micromirrors and functions as a programable multi-object slit for the space-based spectrograph being developed. A high degree of reliability is required for space born devices and these tests will ensure the device meets the reliability requirements.

For this project, the co-op student will be assembling an opto-mechanical system for these tests and developing the control and analysis software. Programing in Python will be required for the operation of the tests and the analysis of the results.

The challenge will be for the student to be able to develop a system to verify the functionally of the DMD devices and exercise the devices to measure their reliability. The reward will be contributing to the success of a future space mission which will enhance our understanding of the universe.

Length of Term

This is a «16 week» term.

Anticipated dates: starting Monday, 5 May 2025, ending Friday, 22 August 2025.

Your Responsibilities

As a student working for the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre in Victoria, British Columbia, your duties will include:

Support a multi-disciplinary engineering and research team
Assemble an opto-mechanical system to test the DMD devices.
Develop code in python to verify the operation of the DMD devices.
Operate the test setup to measure the reliablity of the DMD devices.
Document all work and results in Powerpoint, Excel and Word, as appropriate.
Present your work to the research team.

Condition of Employment

Reliability Status

Salary Range

From $833 to $1,107 per week (37.5 hrs); salaries are determined based on the student's work term.

First $833

Notes

Familiarity with optics, optical assemblies and/or optical mechanical design.

The Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and UV Research (CASTOR) is a planned Canadian-led space observatory which will survey the ultraviolet and blue-optical skies in the 2030s, changing forever our understanding of numerous astronomical and astrophysical events from the birth of stars to their deaths in supernovae, to the rise of supermassive black holes over cosmic timescales. This work is part of the technology development program at HAA to develop the technology for a space-based spectrograph to be flown on the CASTOR mission.

Task - For this project, the co-op student will design upgrades to an existing Ultraviolet (UV) test system to allow testing of new spectrograph components. One of these upgrades is a point-spread-function (PSF) test unit which will generate a targeted beam of UV light, i.e., a "spot", with a width of about 10 microns. This apparatus will be used to determine the PSF of a state-of-the-art UV detector and measure the intra-pixel capacitance, charge diffusion and secondary photon effects. As the wavelength of the light is in Far UV, which is absorbed in air, the test must be done in the vacuum. Thus, this test system must be designed to operate in a vacuum environment.

The PSF test unit will include a collimator, pinhole, and UV re-imaging lens for generating the illuminated spot and an integrating sphere for flux. The student will develop mechanical models for these test systems upgrades, and also the mechanical design of the optical bench which will be holding the optics. The student may prepare fabrication drawings and select commercial components, and, as a goal, be involved in assembling the test unit.

The challenge will be for the student to design upgrades to the system which meet functional requirements, are vacuum compatible and fit within the existing test system. The reward will be contributing to the success of a future space mission which will enhance our understanding of the universe.

Length of Term

This is a «16 week» term.

Anticipated dates: starting Monday, 5 May 2025, ending Friday, 22 August 2025.

Responsibilities

As a student working for the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory in Victoria, British Columbia, your duties will include:

Support a multi-disciplinary engineering and research team.
Develop CAD models of the existing test system.
Design upgrades to the test system such as the PSF test unit ( this working includes developing the design requirement, CAD modeling, integrating off the sheff components where possible and producing fabrication drawings).
Document all work and results in Powerpoint, Excel and Word, as appropriate.
Present your work to the research team.

Fonctions

La Direction de la méthodologie de Statistique Canada est à la recherche d'étudiants pour assister des statisticiens-mathématiciens et scientifique des données responsables de différentes tâches reliées à la production de statistiques officielles et/ou de recherche connexe.

Plusieurs tâches différentes pourraient être offertes à l'étudiant selon les besoins du statisticien-mathématicien ou du scientifique des données et/ou du projet et des connaissances de l'étudiant.

Les tâches sont diverses et peuvent toucher à n'importe lequel des champs suivants : apprentissage automatisé, intelligence artificielle générative, informatique en nuage, exploration de données, traitement de données non-structurées (p. ex. images, texte), création et maintien de bases de sondage, plans d'échantillonnage, collecte de données, vérification et imputation des données, traitement de la non-réponse, estimation des paramètres d'intérêt et de leur variance, analyse des données, mesure des erreurs d'observation, protection de la confidentialité, contrôle et assurance de la qualité, couplage d'enregistrements, simulations empiriques, séries chronologiques ou 'évaluation d'enquête.

Des descriptions de postes plus précises seront envoyées aux étudiants embauchés suite à un processus d'appariement entre les forces des différents étudiants et les besoins des postes à combler.

	

Duties

The Methodology Branch at Statistics Canada is looking for students to assist statistician-mathematicians and responsible for different tasks related to the production of official statistics and/or related research.

Many different tasks could be assigned to the student depending on the needs of the statistician-mathematician and/or the project, and the knowledge of the student.

The tasks are varied and can be in any of the following fields: survey frame creation and maintenance, sample design, edit and imputation of data, treatment of non-response, estimation of parameters of interest and their variance, data analysis, measurement of non-sampling errors, protection of confidentiality, quality control/assurance, record linkage, empirical simulations, time series or survey evaluation.

job_description:
https://leelab-utoronto.com/

If membranes were able to fuse spontaneously, chaos would result. The merger of trillions of vesicles, organelles, and cells would eliminate compartmentalization, cellularity, and life itself. Fortunately, the energy barriers related to membrane deformation and fusion are high, thus two membranes cannot spontaneously merge. Our laboratory is interested in understanding membrane fusion in viral entry and reproductive biology.

Viral entry: entry of enveloped viruses, such as influenza A, HIV-1, SARS-CoV-2, and Ebola virus and others, utilize viral glycoproteins on its surface to mediate cellular attachment, tropism, and viral-host membrane fusion. Dramatic conformational changes in the glycoproteins, triggered through pH-dependent, pH-independent, or two-step mechanisms, are necessary for fusion. We are interested in understanding the molecular mechanisms of viral-cell membrane fusion in order to develop new antivirals that block viral entry.

Sperm-egg fusion: The fusion of membranes is also important in many biological processes, such as fertilization (sperm-egg fusion). The mechanisms of cell-cell fusion are poorly defined and have generally been based on the mechanisms employed by viruses for fusion. Our lab has been active in this research area and are currently funded by a Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation Grand Challenges grant to develop novel non-hormonal contraceptives.

The co-op student will assist laboratory members in cloning expression constructs, protein expression in mammalian or bacterial cultures, protein purification, biophysical and/or structural studies (surface plasmon resonance, biolayer interferometry, crystallography, SAXS). Good laboratory practice, note keeping, attention to detail, work ethic, and punctuality are a must. Previous experience in a biochemistry research lab or students who are interested in pursuing graduate school is a plus.

Students pursuing a Honours degree in Biochemistry will be given priority.

Join us in providing cutting edge data management and data analytics services hosted in the cloud. Our products include SAP HANA Cloud (an in-memory relational database) and SAP Data Lake (which combines the computing speed of an in-memory database with the huge data capacity of a traditional disk-based database). Our services run both on SAP's proprietary cloud and on hyperscalers like AWS, Azure and GCP.

Running in the cloud means using the latest technologies to enable running at huge scale. Our software may be running on thousands of machines, in data centers across the globe. Automation, self-healing algorithms and providing self-serve options are the keys to meeting customer demand for near perfect availability. Creating user instances, rolling out software upgrades, rolling back buggy changes, recovering from hardware and software failures, and monitoring performance and load are just some of the things we need to automate using microservices. This work offers tremendous opportunities to learn cloud technologies such as Go, Kubernetes operators, Docker, AWS, Azure and GCP.

If you want to learn, build, and contribute to cloud software and database technology this is the job for you. We are looking for people who are passionate about learning and problem solving. Job Title: Co-op Student - Geomatics - May/Summer 2025

Job ID: 51980580

Application Deadline: February 9, 2025

What you'll do

Candidate selection, interviews and hiring will take place continuously from this single posting - this means while there is a closing date listed, hiring managers will regularly review applications submitted shortly after the posting is live in your Co-op system. Perform a variety of practical, hands-on work experience directly related to Geomatics.
Learning and training opportunities, including opportunities to network with your division.
Learn all about other divisions and initiatives at BC Hydro.
Take advantage of the opportunity to explore future career options.
Participate in high value, multi-disciplinary project work and gain valuable insight into the organization and implementation of large capital projects. Gain exposure to the exciting and increasingly growing hydro electric industry.

Our ideal candidate can adapt and learn new principles and concepts in a dynamic technical environment, demonstrates a commitment to excellent customer service, and a strong work ethic.

Performs a variety of GIS and remote sensing tasks to complete mapping/geospatial projects, including: researching, selecting and evaluating map source data; preparing and revising maps; applying GIS tools and scripts to manipulate vector and raster datasets; editing and cleaning geospatial datasets based on topological rules; editing and updating web apps and maps.
Identifying and resolving source document and spatial data conflicts and updating information to ensure accuracy of data.
Performing data analysis, queries, and cartographic data visualization using a variety of computer languages and programs, such as ArcPro and FME.
Assisting with the development and implementation of quality control procedures, visual output standards, and in-house procedures
Verifying and checking data to ensure continuity, integrity and compliance with standards; compiling, enhancing and digitizing source information for the creation of various resource themes, databases, spatial products and related models.

As a condition of employment at BC Hydro, a background check clearance will be required.
All positions will be hired first as a four month work term. For some positions, there is opportunity to extend, to eight months.
May accept applications from students who are enrolled in and who have not yet graduated from a recognized post secondary institution and who may not be enrolled in a co-op program.

Experience with ESRI software suite (ArcPro, ArcGIS Enterprise, Portal for ArcGIS, Web AppBuilder / Experience Builder, Image Analyst) is an asset.

Strong communication skills, highly motivated and results oriented.

THE DETAILS

Work term Options: Summer 2025 (May to August) or Summer and Fall 2025 (May to December)

Office Location: 750 Pandora Avenue, Victoria, BC
Spend your off hours exploring beautiful Victoria and Vancouver Island
All co-ops/internships will need to be completed in person at our Victoria office with the option to work one day per week from home. Please note, some positions are not eligible for hybrid work.

Step into the forefront of investment operations innovation with the British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI) in Victoria, BC. We are eagerly seeking a forward-thinking Cash Management Co-op/intern, available for a preference for an eight-month term Summer and Fall 2025 placement (May to December) or the possibility of a four-month term for the Summer 2025 work term (May to August). This is a pivotal time to join us, as our team transitions to becoming active managers of cash and the primary voice in short-term funding decisions within the organization. If you are passionate about contributing to significant financial management strategies and being part of a rapidly evolving team, this opportunity is for you.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
BCI manages a globally diversified portfolio of assets valued at $250.4 billion and is one of Canada's largest institutional investors. We invest globally to support pension and other funds for more than 30 clients based in British Columbia. We are proud to have been chosen as one of Canada's Top 100 Employers and BC's Top Employers. These national and provincial competitions recognize employers who offer exceptional workplaces for their employees.

In this transformative phase, our Cash Management team within the Investment Operations department is taking a proactive stance in managing client liquidity and shaping the organization's short-term funding strategies. As a co-op/intern, you will support high volumes of complex cash activities, contribute to the development of reports, create concise documentation, and assist in cash reconciliation. Additionally, you will step in on key tasks, ensuring the smooth functioning of our operations amid rapid technological advancements.

WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH

Investment Operations (IO) is comprised of four branches: Derivatives, Collateral & Engineering, Trade Management, Cash Operations and Business Solutions. The department delivers core capabilities in areas including trade settlements, corporate actions, derivatives, collateral management, foreign exchange, and cash services, while collaborating with internal partners to design and coordinate end-to-end solutions and providing leadership for the custodian relationship.

The Cash Management team is part of the Cash Operations branch and is accountable for optimizing cash balances for clients and asset classes. This team focuses on delivering BCI clients and asset classes with expertise on funding, minimizing transaction costs, and maximizing netting opportunities to meet obligations and support value add strategies.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

Supporting the management of complex cash activities amidst our evolving technical infrastructure
Creating detailed reports and developing concise documentation to support cash management processes
Executing testing procedures and stepping in on key operational tasks as necessary
Contributing to the team's transformation into active cash management and short-term funding decision-making
Prepare weekly and monthly reports for the department and management teams
Ad-hoc projects and tasks as assigned by the team

WHAT WE OFFER

A dynamic, supportive team environment where innovation is encouraged
Development of practical skills in financial and liquidity management in a leading financial institution
Exposure to some of the most talented, approachable, and inspiring people in the industry
The ability to opt-in for access to Dialogue, a user-friendly app that offers virtual primary care, employee and family services, and mental health supports
Time to connect with co-op students & interns at BCI - build your network and shared learning
BCI investment professionals lead a monthly Investment Club to share industry knowledge with employees who work in other departments
2 paid days per year for volunteering
Competitive pay: Mid / Back Office: $2,260.00 gross bi-weekly or $2,090.00 gross bi-weekly + vacation leave paid based on 6% of salary ($2,260.00 gross biweekly for those with (or working towards) a graduate degree or joining the Investment Strategy & Risk department and $2,090.00 gross biweekly for those with (or working towards) an undergraduate degree, diploma, or certificate)
Travel: if coming to Victoria for this work term, BCI will provide a fixed-rate travel allowance based on your location

DCS VALIDATION ENGINEER CO-OP

Division: DCS Arch & Validation

The System Engineering group is responsible for ensuring that the end products operate fully in their intended applications. This involves the planning, design, integration, test and documentation of a complete system level platform used to test the prototype System-on-Chip (Soc) along with associated Firmware (FW) & Software (SW). The System Validation Engineer works in parallel with IC and FW engineers to design an appropriate test system. This can involve test FW development, FPGA VHDL/Verilog coding, digital/analog board designs and test script coding.

Using these systems, together with the latest communication analyzers and test equipment, the System Validation Design Engineer will execute a Feature Test Plan that fully validates all features of the prototype SoC and associated FW. The System Validation Design Engineer will be involved with existing and newly drafted standards used in Cloud Storage, Data Center and other high performance computing applications such as including PCIe, NVMe and others.

Responsibilities

As a Validation Engineer Co-Op, you would be assigned one or more of these activities:

Designing, building and debugging complete systems designed to test Hardware, Software & Firmware.
Develop new software and/or hardware tools to aid in automation, testing & debug
Application level Tcl/Tk scripting for automated control of the test systems
Troubleshoot and resolve problems related to test setup configuration & validation test failures.
Installing & configuration of server operating systems.
Operate basic lab equipment to measure performance & analyze device behavior
Present technical information to small teams of engineers.

You will work as part of a team to develop, execute and document a series of Feature Tests that will fully validate the operation of the prototype SoC as part of the overall system. These feature tests will exercise the various functional blocks of a prototype IC & associated FW/SW to ensure the system meets designed criteria and industry standards.

Ability to read basic electronic circuit schematics

Knowledge of Computer Interconnect Protocols (e.g. PCIe, I2C, SPI, TCP/IP, etc)

Company description
Nexera Robotics is a robotics company that is solving one of the most fundamental problems in the field of robotics. For decades the inability of robots to reliably grasp diverse objects (an apple, a shopping bag, a hairbrush, etc.) has severely limited their deployment outside of well-structured environments like automated assembly lines (car manufacturing). Nexera Robotics has developed a novel and patented grasping platform technology that is fundamentally capable of securely grasping a hugely diverse range of objects.

We have funding and a core technical team for the next stage of development who will be on site to support you. The primary aspects of the technology have been refined and validated over the previous few years in a university research lab, and Nexera Robotics is now focused on the rapid commercialization of the technology.

Our office and lab are in North Vancouver by the second narrows bridge. We are looking for strong aspiring computer scientists and engineers, with diverse skillsets, who have the drive and energy to be part of the early stage of a fast-moving company.

There are massive opportunities to be a part of a growing venture during the coop placement and beyond.

Where will you fit in?
As part of a tight-knit team, your primary role will be as part of the R&D team in extending the capabilities of our proprietary grasping software application.

You may also assist the team to integrate our robot and technology with third-party vision systems and software to ensure our technology can meet the needs of multiple market segments.

The role will be highly adapted to the strengths of the candidate.

We want to ensure that you get the best experience from this placement and will be supporting you throughout with regular reviews and feedback.

Main Activities (Roles and Responsibilities)

Development of software tools related to our grasping technology
Development of applications for enabling 24/7 robotic testing
Assist in data collection and labelling, including design and running of experiments
Data analysis of test results
Working with Robot Manipulators
Coding and modifying testing protocols while interfacing with peripheral devices (e.g., cameras, sensors, robots and controllers/drives)
Helping with day-to-day tasks to push the company forward faster
Many other possible tasks depending on candidates' native skills

Position: Materials Technician

Start Month and Duration: May start, 8-month term

General Overview:

Almor Testing Services Ltd. (Almor) is a geotechnical and materials testing consultant, based in Calgary, Alberta. Almor provides geotechnical consulting and materials testing services to land developers, general contractors, municipalities, and other consultants. Projects Almor participates in include residential and commercial developments and civil infrastructure upgrades/improvements. Almor's role onsite varies, but includes preliminary geotechnical investigations, consulting, and QC/QA testing of materials.

Student(s) hired will perform field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and asphalt materials, and be expected to keep accurate and organized records of test results, calibrations, site observations and billable hours.

Daily Activities:

Laboratory Work (soils and concrete) - Student technicians will perform ASTM and CSA test procedures, record keeping and facilities/equipment maintenance (light duty cleaning, equipment calibrations, etc.). Lab tests on soils are typically part of an overall process used to identify soil types and engineering properties, which are then used to develop project specifications or confirm compliance with specifications. Lab work with concrete involves technical measurements, record keeping and testing of compressive strength specimens.

Field Work (soils, concrete, and asphalt) - Student technicians will participate in compaction monitoring/testing during civil construction, which involves the use of a nuclear moisture/density gauge to measure the density of soils and asphalt. Concrete testing involves slump and air tests, as well as the casting of compressive strength samples. Students will be working with clients and contractors in a QC/QA role to ensure compliance with project specifications. This will involve following ASTM and CSA test methods, awareness of project specifications and standards, as well as record keeping and communication of results to clients, contractors, and supervisors.

Training Provided:

Company orientation(s)
Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG)
Generic and Worksite specific WHMIS
Construction Safety Training System (CSTS)
Task specific training
Additional training and orientations, as required

Skills Obtained or Improved:

Written and verbal communications through record keeping and daily activity documentations
Time management skills through opportunities to co-ordinate with clients/contractors and multitask with lab and field work
Exposure to professional/client/contractor relationships

Equipment/Materials Provided by Almor:

Personal Protective Equipment
Stationary
Private locker
Work vehicle and test equipment

Students Must Provide:

CSA certified protective footwear

Almor Work Culture:

Almor has been employing co-op students for more than 30 years. We provide a casual environment where students regularly earn overtime hours from week to week. Throughout the work term there are opportunities to socialize at events held at the office (BBQ's/dinners, bowling/sport events, etc.) and long-term connections with students from other institutions and programs are often made during these co-op terms.

Almor's supervisors are keen to provide a challenging, safe, and informative work environment.

You do not need to have previous experience with ultrasound. You will be involved in applying modern deep learning research in areas such as supervised, self-supervised, reinforcement, and representation learning for ultrasound imaging modalities.

You will actively participate in industrial scientific research focused on state-of-the-art ultrasound imaging solutions. You will be working in a multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers dedicated to advancing ultrasound technology. The ideal candidate is both scientifically minded and pragmatic, with a strong desire to work and grow in a fast-paced technology environment.

Innovate: Engage in cutting-edge research, implementing, and developing state-of-the-art deep learning models.

Deploy: Learn how to deploy ML algorithms to end-users, continuously monitor the performance to identify opportunities for improvement.

Collaborate: Work closely with fellow scientists and engineers within the team who will mentor you and support your endeavors. Collaborate within and outside of DarkVision to achieve research objectives.

Communicate: Prepare and deliver presentations and/or technical reports showcasing your work to different audiences.

Applying deep learning to real world industrial datasets containing billions of data points such as images and knowledge bases

Working with severely imbalanced datasets

Latest advancements in deep learning

Scalable cloud infrastructure using AWS

Converting ideas into intellectual property assets (e.g., patents)

DarkVision Technologies Inc. is a Canada-based tech company disrupting the industrial imaging market since 2013. We have created the world's most advanced acoustic-based imaging platform. We are packaging it into multiple new product lines, revolutionizing how our clients quantify and visualize the integrity of their critical assets.

Backed by Koch Industries, one of the world's largest privately held companies, Darkvision's team of Mechanical, Skunkworks, Electrical, Software, and Machine Learning Engineers is rapidly expanding to meet the demand for the company's current and upcoming products. Our employees to work on cutting-edge technologies that blend science with real-world applications.

Collaborating with scientists to gather and translate user requirements into effective data processing functions.
Reviewing and maintaining code, debugging issues and implementing new features to improve system functionality.

Acquire experience in a sector dedicated to sustainability, energy efficiency, and smart building solutions.

Casual dress

Personal days together with sick and vacation days

About Osoyoos Desert Centre
On the southern edge of British Columbia's beautiful Okanagan valley is one of Canada's most critically endangered ecosystems - the semi-arid, antelope-brush shrub-steppe. In the 1990s a group of concerned citizens eager to protect, restore and advocate for our disappearing desert environment opened the Osoyoos Desert Centre, a 67-acre nature interpretive facility.

At the heart of our mission is the desire to provide engaging, immersive experiences in nature, offering insight into our natural world and inspiring active concern for healthy ecosystems. Each year we welcome thousands of visitors from around the world, who take tours along our 1.5 km boardwalk trail, enjoy interactive displays in our interpretive discovery centre, and gain landscaping inspiration from our native plant garden. Through various educational initiatives, visitors learn about biodiversity loss, habitat connectivity, climate change and invasive species management, and take part in hands-on workshops like creating pollinator gardens or building bluebird nest boxes. We are also keen to deliver outdoor, place-based educational field trips to hundreds of students each year, working with teachers to tie learning outcomes to BC's education curriculum.

Conservation Guide

ODC Conservation Guides act as ambassadors of ODC, embodying our mission and values in every interaction and representing the organization with enthusiasm, professionalism, and dedication. ODC Conservation Guides create exceptional visitor experiences by providing education and information, sharing knowledge and stories, and creating lifelong memories. ODC provides comprehensive training to facilitate learning the role of Conservation Guide, ensuring our staff acquire the skills and knowledge to excel at this position and beyond, creating their own lifelong memories.

Key Responsibilities
Public education

• Lead guided tours for the general public, private tour groups and school groups

• Learn and effectively communicate wildlife and habitat information

• Conduct presentations on local flora and fauna

• Assist at special events including workshops and seminars

Scientific Monitoring and Data Collection

• Monitor water levels in spadefoot breeding ponds and fill as per schedule

• Monitor hummingbird feeders and clean/fill as per schedule

• Monitor bluebird boxes and record bluebird data

• Participate in ongoing ODC data collection and research projects including Behr's Hairstreak Surveys

• Record species sightings (iNaturalist)

• Update log sheets (water, feeders, etc.)

Customer Service

• Interact with visitors following tours and in the Interpretive Building exhibit area

• Cover admissions desk duties (admissions and merchandise sales) as needed

• Provide local, national and international visitors with information about the local area

• Source information in field guides, tour books, etc. to assist visitors

Cleaning and Site Maintenance

• Invasive plant remediation, landscape pruning and weeding

• Clean and re-stock interpretive building, gift shop and bathroom

• Empty garbage and recycling, pick up litter, sweep walkways, etc.

Previous conservation guide experience is not necessary. We provide comprehensive on-the-job training. We are seeking candidates who possess the following qualities and skills:

• A keen interest in science, education, and/or nature interpretation

• Outgoing personality and excellent interpersonal, intercultural, and intergenerational communication skills

• Ability to work effectively within a team as well as work independently with minimal supervision

• Ability to learn and integrate new information

• Confidence in educating and inspiring groups of people through public speaking

• Ability to make sound judgments and respond tactfully in various situations

• Self-directed, organized and adept at multitasking, prioritization, and problem-solving

• Interest in working with a dynamic and collaborative group of individuals and gaining hands-on skills

Requirements

• Valid class 5 driver's license and access to a reliable vehicle.

HOURS: 35 hours per week; some evening and weekend work is required

TERM: May to August; 1 position to extend to October if possible

WAGE: $20/hour

LOCATION: Osoyoos BC, on-site

Highly organized and the capability to plan and prioritize independently
Excellent written and verbal communication skills to a wide range of audiences

We are an organization comprised of industry thought leaders who are passionate about health data and want to make a difference in the health care field. We are an independent, not-for-profit organization and together with our partners we provide essential information on Canada's health systems, enabling decisions that lead to healthier Canadians. Project Description

The HCTF (Hot Cold Test Facility) is used to measure the noise temperature of radio receivers. This is accomplished by taking a series of "hot/cold" measurements where an absorber lined roof is closed over the receiver for "hot" measurements and then opened to allow the "cold" sky to be measured. These measurements often span over days and sometimes require measurements outside working hours.

The current system is controlled through a Python script which opens and closes the roof, takes absorber temperature and copies spectrum traces from the spectrum analysers. It has been found that this script contains many redundancies which sometimes lead to the system being unreliable. Furthermore this script was done in Python2 which is no longer supported. The current process is also not user friendly with variables needing to be defined throughout the script. There currently does not exist a means to monitor the device under test or a means to do remote measurements.

Length of Term

This is a «16 week» term.

Anticipated dates: starting Monday, 5 May 2025, ending Friday, 22 August 2025.

Clean up the HCTF control script
Extensive system testing to make sure it runs reliably.
Create a user friendly interface as well as writing an operator manual.
Implement and integrate monitoring capabilities which could be done using a LabJack or similar device.
Implement additional remote monitor and control capabilities to add safeguards to address system failure or changing weather conditions.

* The Employment Equity Act, which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.

Candidates are asked to self-declare when applying to this hiring process.

Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre is very keen on engaging with diverse groups, including Indigenous students, in science, technology, and engineering through professional opportunities, as it values diversity of backgrounds, lenses, knowledges, experiences and perspectives, which enriches and nurtures collaboration and innovation. The merging of knowledge within a team is definitively considered as a strong asset by the organization. Indigenous students will be encouraged to discuss with their supervisor on how the organization can support them in their learning and working experience.

City: Penticton

Organizational Unit: Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics

Discover the possible

Anything is possible at the National Research Council (NRC). As Canada's leading research and technology organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada's future and the world.

At the NRC, you'll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You'll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you'll discover what's possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

Project Description

The Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) radio telescope, situated on Wajarri Yamaji Country in Western Australia, is one of the best instruments in the world for mapping the sky at radio wavelengths. The Polarization Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM) is a project that is using ASKAP to study magnetic fields in various environments across the Universe, through synchrotron radiation and its associated Faraday rotation. A key concept is the measurement of Faraday rotation measures (RMs), a property of radio sources that tells us the strength and direction of magnetic fields along the line of sight. The enormous data volume of POSSUM poses a huge processing challenge requiring innovative solutions to achieve this unprecedented magnetic picture of the Universe.

The student will work with Dr. Jennifer West to write code that leverages super computing resources available through the Canadian Astronomy Data Centre (CADC), operated by NRC HAA, and contribute to a pipeline that will be used to create the world's best catalogue of polarization measurements. The student will then perform scientific analysis on these processed data and will work on a project with the goal of understanding the large scale structure of the magnetic field of our own Milky Way Galaxy and/or other galaxies. The student will spend about 50% of their time each on the technical and scientific aspects of this project.

Length of Term

This is a «16 week» term.

Anticipated dates: starting Monday, 5 May 2025, ending Friday, 22 August 2025.

Responsibilities

Write and/or use existing code to process data from the ASKAP Telescope and assess the data quality
Use CADC computing resources to perform data processing tasks and test/develop new methods of processing.
Write/improve documentation for other users.
Work on a science project utilizing ASKAP radio polarization data.

salary: $15.75 hourly for35 hours per week
job_description:
Undergraduate (4 months) and Graduate research positions are available in the Nonlinear Photonics Group at l'Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique (INRS), in the Énergie, Matériaux, et Télécommunications (EMT) center.

About INRS:

INRS, the research-oriented branch of Université du Québec, is renowned as a top Canadian research university in terms of publication and research intensity ($ per graduate student (rank 1 in Canada) and $ per faculty (rank 2 in Canada) - RESEARCH Infosource 2019). Our center (INRS-EMT) is devoted to the development of cutting-edge research programs in a variety of technological areas, including photonics, nanotechnologies, and telecommunications. Following a strong development of our facilities, we are now equipped with state-of-the-art laboratories and instruments (worth over $100 million) for device fabrication and characterization. For more information on our Center, please visit: http://www.emt.inrs.ca.

About the research:

Prof. Morandotti's group is currently investigating innovative approaches in photonics based on various free space and integrated technologies. Our work (reported on in journals such as Physical Review Letters, Science, the Nature series, - Nature, Nature Photonics, Nature Physics, Nature Communication, etc. - and recognized with several prestigious awards) involves both theory and experimental work - as well as several industrial links. For more information on our group, please visit: www.nonlinearphotonics.com.

Note: Undergraduate students in their final year of study are especially encouraged to apply.

Project sample and titles

Project 1: AI-driven terahertz integrated signal-processing chips

Research Project: The Nonlinear Photonics Group at INRS-EMT, under the guidance of Prof. Roberto Morandotti, is actively engaged in pushing the boundaries of the captivating and emerging field of THz communications. Our primary focus lies in exploring innovative device concepts for wave guiding, modulation, multiplexing, and wavefront engineering. This project entails the development of cost-effective, robust, and highly reconfigurable THz integrated chips, marking a first-time endeavor for the team. These chips will serve as a versatile platform for signal-processing functionalities, leveraging the power of inverse photonic design augmented by machine learning (ML) algorithms. This unique approach will unlock unprecedented multifunctional capabilities in the THz domain. The fabrication of these machine-learning-enabled devices will utilize cutting-edge additive manufacturing techniques, such as 3D printing. The resulting integrated chips will offer a versatile and robust broadband solution, addressing critical challenges in THz signal processing while showcasing their potential for future applications in wireless networking.

Role of the Student: The student will work with cutting-edge THz photonic equipment, in particular, ultrafast lasers and photoconductive antennas. The student will be also co-supervised by PhD students and postdoctoral fellows. The student will gain expertise in THz photonics and understand how to apply ML algorithms into THz photonic devices and systems. The main tasks for the student's role are:

- Experimental training for the generation and detection of the THz waves.

- Establish the THz system for characterizing the THz devices.

- Design of an integrated THz chip driven by the concept of inverse design powered by ML algorithms. Refine the output of the design by exploring different ML algorithms.

- Fabricate the THz chip using 3D printing techniques and characterize the chip using the state-of-the-art THz systems.

- Automate/interface with instruments as well as the optical components (such as lock-in amplifiers, arbitrary waveform generators, etc.) with electronics using MATLAB or LabVIEW.

Project 2: Photonic lattices for multilayer artificial neural networks

Research Project: This project aims to explore the potential of photonic lattices for the realization of a multilayer ANNs, for smart photonic applications with a focus on ultra-fast all-optical signal processing. The ANNs will be trained using supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms. The construction of the photonic lattices will involve optical coupled fibers and different lattice geometries. By exploiting the periodic interaction of optical pulses at the coupling points, an NxM dimensional lattice will be generated. The exchange of information between interacting pulses will form the optical nodes (neurons) of the photonic ANN, with weighted connections the adjust the strength of propagating signals. Output signals will be readout using photodetectors and oscilloscopes. Theoretical investigation of this ANN concept is crucial to establish its feasibility and serve as a proof of concept for a viable realization. A successful project outcome will contribute to paving the way for real-world applications, such as ANN-assisted signal processing for speech and image recognition and telecom signal equalization.

Role of the Student: The candidate will engage in the field of nonlinear optics, specifically focusing on the modelling of photonic lattices for the development of SD. The primary objective will be to study the network behaviour through comprehensive numerical simulations, considering various system parameters such as coupling geometry, dimensions, and input signals. This will enable a thorough characterization of the network and provide valuable insights into its potential for real-world applications. The student will also benefit from co-supervision by experienced PhD students and postdoctoral fellows. The project will offer the opportunity to develop expertise in nonlinear photonics and gain a deep understanding of in ML and ANNs methodologies, nonlinear systems modelling, and numerical solvers. In summary, the main tasks for the candidate will involve:

- Modeling synthetic dimensions using coupled optical photonic lattices.

- Conducting numerical simulations to study the behavior of the system and its parameters.

- Exploring different coupling geometries and understanding the relationship between geometries and artificial neural network topologies.

- Applying concepts of machine learning (ML) to train the resulting photonic ANN.

- Benchmarking the system for real-world applications, evaluating its performance and potential.

Project 3: Quantum-enhanced multi-parameter estimation in synthetic photonic lattices

Project Description: The proposed project focuses on harnessing quantum photonic architectures for both quantum metrology and quantum walk applications (refers to the movement of a quantum particle within a discrete space, such as a network or lattice of nodes). The aim is to utilize these architectures to enable high-precision multi-parameter estimations. To achieve this, the project will employ high-dimensional quantum-entangled states, which offer numerous advantages including improved noise resilience, increased information capacity, and reduced complexities in setup and measurement. Specifically, the project will emphasize the use of two- and four-dimensional entangled states in the temporal domain, which will serve as a reliable and user-friendly platform for simultaneous multi-parameter estimation.

Role of the Student: The student will have an exciting opportunity to work with state-of-the-art equipment, including high-efficiency superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, high-speed time-to-digital converters, and high-quality quantum photonic sources. They will benefit from co-supervision by PhD students and postdoctoral fellows, allowing for guidance while also encouraging independent work. The tasks assigned to the student encompass the following:

- Gaining a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical aspects related to various quantum walk strategies employed to process high-dimensional quantum states and estimate the associated limits of sensitivity.

- Constructing the optical setup required for the planned experiment on quantum-enhanced multi-parameter estimation.

- Developing a programming interface to remotely control the experimental setup

Salary

Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada: Undergraduate Student Research Awards and compensated by Prof. Morandotti to provide the minimum salary in Quebec ($15.75/ hr.)

job_description:
Job Description


The Staples Lab at the University of British Columbia is seeking a full-time graduate-level Data Analyst to work on a portfolio of exciting grant-funded research projects that use British Columbia's unique linked population-based administrative data to address pressing public health problems. The position start date is May 2025. The successful applicant will gain valuable experience in cleaning and linking research data, preparing an analytic data set, selecting and implementing appropriate statistical methodologies, creating compelling data visualizations, and communicating scientific results.


We have a few ongoing projects in the lab. One potential project is entitled "Reducing harms associated with 'before medical advised' (BMA) hospital discharge", that seeks to reduce the risks of adverse events (such as ED visit, unplanned readmission, drug overdose, death) that are linked with BMA discharges. This project examines the trends in BMA discharge and the harms associated with BMA discharge over the last two decades in British Columbia using population-based linked administrative health datasets. We also evaluate whether specific post-discharge interventions (e.g., early outpatient clinician follow-up, return to hospital, outpatient prescription medication fills) can reduce these harms in 30 days following BMA discharge, using cohort study designs and cutting-edge target trial emulation techniques. Using a Monte Carlo simulation model, we will model the absolute and relative reductions in population-level harms that might be achieved by scaling up promising clinical interventions. Our overarching goal is to inform the clinical and public health response on the adverse events linked with BMA discharge, including its impact on the accelerating opioid overdose crisis.
The successful applicant will be supervised by study Principal Investigator (PI) Dr. John A Staples MD FRCPC MPH, a Clinical Associate Professor in the UBC Department of Medicine. The successful candidate should be able to work independently, collaborate with other members of the Staples Lab and with the affiliated UBC Road Safety Research Team, and communicate clearly and concisely in written and oral form.


The successful applicant must work in accordance with UBC's scholarly integrity policies and practice data integrity. They are required to conduct all research activities in an ethical manner, suited to the proper activities of Vancouver General Hospital and UBC as well as to the professional organizations governing his or herself and those governing the activities of the PI and other investigators. Medical records and health data are highly confidential and must be handled with the utmost discretion. These records are released only to select study staff and only for the purposes of the study. Intentional or unintentional breaches of privacy and confidentiality may result in study termination, loss of study funding, or termination of employment and may prompt an administrative or criminal investigation.


Equity and diversity are essential to academic excellence. An open and diverse community fosters the inclusion of voices that have been underrepresented or discouraged. We encourage applications from members of groups that have been marginalized on any grounds enumerated under the B.C. Human Rights Code, including sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, racialization, disability, political belief, religion, marital or family status, age, and / or status as a First Nation, Metis, Inuit, or Indigenous person. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.


The successful applicant will have the flexibility for a hybrid work schedule, to work remotely or in-person at our Vancouver General Hospital research site.

• Knowledge of commonly used statistical analyses in health research and epidemiology, including model building for survival analysis, mixed effects models, and logistic regression, and the development and validation of predictive models.
• Ability and interest in learning new statistical techniques if required for any projects.
• Superb oral and written English communication skills, including demonstrated excellence in academic writing.
• Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.

BKL Consultants Ltd. (BKL) is currently seeking a co-op student who has a demonstrated interest in the field of acoustics. If you have taken some relevant courses in sound or vibration, or have relevant background or experience, we'd love to hear from you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO/DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Each employee at BKL works on multiple different architectural and/or environmental projects. As an acoustical engineering intern, you will be working under a number of different acoustical consultants throughout the internship and will be exposed to acoustical work in various industries and sectors.

We will provide the training necessary for you to carry out various duties but we will also expect the student to research some aspects of the job independently, with guidance from other team members.

In any given day may consist of the following work:

Programming and setting up noise or vibration monitoring systems in the field;
Carrying out exterior and interior noise calculations;
Preparing proposals, memos, letters, and reports for routine types of projects;
Refining systems for managing acoustical products, software, and instrumentation; and
Assisting other engineers making other types of sound and vibration measurements in the field.

Most work is expected to be office-based and at project sites in the Lower Mainland, but brief site visits to other locations in BC may be required.

CO-OP AT BKL

Want to know what your day might look like? Here's a blog about what it's like to be a co-op student at BKL.

ABOUT US

As British Columbia's premier acoustical consultancy since it opened its doors more than 50 years ago, BKL works with governments, facility owners, and consultants to provide accurate acoustics, noise, and vibration assessments and solutions. BKL's team of 17 acoustical engineers and scientists has more than 150 years of accumulated experience in acoustics. An extensive complement of specialized instrumentation and software supports the technical staff. Further details are provided on our web site at www.bkl.ca

Zephyr firmware routines to evaluate system integrity in the field
electronic circuitry and software to validate in-house microelectronic module performance
infrastructure and routines to validate real-world integrity of communications protocols
development of physical (electromechanical) user interfaces
development of digital user interfaces
SDKs and APIs for system tie-in to third-party systems

Support the development and documentation for new or existing features
Review, analyze, and optimize the architecture of the product with innovative solutions
Refine and develop the interfaces between firmware and software
Assess, test, troubleshoot for operating systems and applications software
Collect, document and develop logical and physical specifications
Collaborate with internal stakeholders from various team

Career Development And Training:

Gain hands-on experience with CAD and ECAD software suites in addition to test and measurement equipment for prototyping both in-house and externally fabricated microelectronic modules
Exposure to contemporary and emergent SDKs and APIs for communication with microelectronic modules;
Develop skills in troubleshooting complex integrated systems;
Communicate technical results effectively to multidisciplinary teams;
Enhance your problem-solving, teamwork, communication, and time management abilities;
Understand the electronic degradation mechanisms of devices and their effects on performance and lifespan;
Develop a high proficiency in Google Workspace ; and
Acquire experience in a sector dedicated to sustainability, energy efficiency, and smart building solutions.

Aside from all of the learning opportunities listed above, here are a few other great reasons to join us for your work term:

Casual dress
Social and wellness activities such as rooftop BBQs and curling
Personal days together with sick and vacation days
